sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue 19th ed., entry 'Ayta, Sorsogon' [ays] (Internet Archive copy of ethnologue.com/language/ays).
sources.note: Nothing. Population 15 (Wurm 2000), ethnic 180; Prieto Diaz, Sorsogon; status 8b Nearly extinct; classified Central Philippine; 'Frequent intermarriage with other groups.' No dialect or grammatical comment.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Mānoa. Section 3.2.20 'Sorsogon "Ayta"', pp. 91-92 (pp. 112-113); status table p. 56ff.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that the Prieto Diaz 'Ayta' are native speakers only of Bikol Legaspi (North Coastal Sorsogon dialect); ancestors reportedly spoke 'differently', but descriptions indicated 'more of a difference in intonational pattern than a difference in language or dialect'; 'No language data is known to exist for whatever language this group might have spoken in the past' (p. 92). Table (p. 56ff.) lists †Sorsogon 'Ayta' as extinct, replaced by Central Bikol (N. Sorsogon) and Tagalog, ø speakers (Lobel 2006 visit).
